# Stargazing Index

> Stargazing Index is a bilingual, data-driven guide for choosing stargazing destinations, months, observing sites, and astronomy gear. Its reviewed field guides, independent routes, and source-backed comparisons are supported by reproducible JSON data and clearly stated limitations.

The primary language is English. German versions use the same paths under `/de/`; each page declares reciprocal language alternates. Destination scores use historical climate normals and darkness data, not live weather. Astronomical sky simulations do not include local clouds, haze, terrain, buildings, vegetation, or measured on-site light pollution. Gear comparisons are editorial analyses of cited manufacturer specifications and do not claim hands-on testing unless explicitly stated.

## Start here

- [English home](https://stargazingindex.com/en/): Browse destinations, short trips, and gear guides.
- [German home](https://stargazingindex.com/de/): Deutsche Übersicht aller Ziele, Kurzreisen und Ausrüstungsguides.
- [About the publisher](https://stargazingindex.com/en/about/): Mission, editorial responsibility, corrections, and ownership.
- [Editorial methodology](https://stargazingindex.com/en/methodology/): Evidence, source, freshness, and independence rules.
- [XML sitemap](https://stargazingindex.com/sitemap.xml): Complete list of indexable English and German canonical pages.

## Destination guides

- [Alqueva stargazing: Cumeada Observatory and a Dark Sky route](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/alqueva/): Plan an Alqueva night around the booked Cumeada Observatory experience, the wider Dark Sky route and realistic rural access in Portugal's Alentejo.
- [Anza-Borrego stargazing: where to observe and when to camp](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/anza-borrego/): Plan an Anza-Borrego stargazing night around verified campground access, desert heat, seasonal closures, dark adaptation, and a safe return to Borrego Springs.
- [Aoraki Mackenzie stargazing: Tekapo, Mt John and a booked night](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/aoraki-mackenzie/): Understand public access at Ōtehīwai Mt John, choose among Mackenzie sky experiences and plan a source-backed Lake Tekapo observing evening.
- [Atacama stargazing from San Pedro: altitude, access and a guided night](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/atacama/): Plan a San Pedro de Atacama astronomy night with altitude-aware timing, protected-area boundaries, guided interpretation and current official sources.
- [Big Bend stargazing: Sotol Vista, road safety and a desert night](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/big-bend/): Plan a Big Bend stargazing evening at NPS-listed Sotol Vista with paved access, current-condition checks, desert safety and an unhurried night route.
- [Bannau Brycheiniog stargazing: Usk Reservoir night plan](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/brecon-beacons/): Plan a Bannau Brycheiniog stargazing night at Usk Reservoir with official site choices, parking, Welsh mountain weather, narrow roads, water protection, and safe timing.
- [Canyonlands stargazing: Island in the Sky without a night-road gamble](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/canyonlands/): Plan a Canyonlands stargazing night on the paved Island in the Sky mesa with legal lighting, current road checks, water and a safe return to Moab.
- [Cherry Springs stargazing: public field, permits and a practical night](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/cherry-springs/): Choose the correct Cherry Springs stargazing area, understand overnight permits and plan a low-light observing session with official Pennsylvania guidance.
- [Death Valley stargazing: Mesquite Flat, heat and a safe night plan](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/death-valley/): Plan an independent Death Valley stargazing night at Mesquite Flat with current road checks, heat limits, legal parking and an unhurried return.
- [Eifel Dark Sky Park: where to observe without disturbing the park](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/eifel/): Plan an Eifel stargazing night at an official SternenBlick or booked Vogelsang event while respecting wildlife, marked routes, parking, weather, and no camping.
- [Elqui Valley stargazing: Mamalluca booking and a Vicuña night](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/elqui-valley/): Plan an Elqui Valley astronomy night around Mamalluca's official booking, Vicuña check-in, transport, lunar timing and realistic independent access.
- [Exmoor stargazing: choose a real observing site, not a map centre](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/exmoor/): Plan an Exmoor dark-sky night at Wimbleball or an official observing site, with parking, narrow roads, weather, land access, red light, and a safe return.
- [Galloway Forest stargazing: Clatteringshaws and a safe night plan](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/galloway/): Plan Galloway stargazing from official Forestry and Land Scotland sites, with current facility notes, a Clatteringshaws route and wet-weather realism.
- [Grasslands National Park stargazing: East or West Block](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/grasslands/): Choose the right Grasslands National Park block and plan a prairie night around Two Trees, Frenchman Valley, gravel roads, bison, rattlesnakes, water, and camping.
- [Great Basin stargazing: Mather Overlook and a mountain night plan](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/great-basin/): Plan a Great Basin stargazing night at Mather Overlook with seasonal road checks, altitude preparation, legal overnight options and NPS sources.
- [Great Sand Dunes stargazing: parking, safety and the best season](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/great-sand-dunes/): Plan a Great Sand Dunes night from the Dunes Parking Area or Piñon Flats, with moon timing, altitude, cold, wildlife, storms, and a safe return route.
- [Jasper stargazing: Pyramid Island and a current-status night plan](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/jasper/): Plan a Jasper dark-sky evening at Pyramid Island with Parks Canada sources, wildfire-recovery checks, wildlife safety and a close-to-town route.
- [Kielder stargazing: observatory booking or forest night](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/kielder/): Plan Kielder stargazing through a booked observatory event or Stonehaugh Pavilion, with forest parking, 3 a.m. limits, dark roads, weather, and quiet access.
- [Kitt Peak stargazing: book the mountain, do not improvise it](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/kitt-peak/): Plan a Kitt Peak night through the official Visitor Center programme, with reservation, mountain-road, altitude, weather and return-drive guidance.
- [Stargazing on La Palma: viewpoints, access and a night route](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/la-palma/): Plan a responsible stargazing night on La Palma with official viewpoints, realistic access notes, a self-guided route and primary sources.
- [Maunakea stargazing: VIS access, altitude and summit rules](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/mauna-kea/): Plan a respectful Maunakea stargazing evening at the Visitor Information Station with clear summit limits, altitude checks and official guidance.
- [McDonald Observatory stargazing: Star Party or independent night](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/mcdonald-observatory/): Compare a reserved McDonald Observatory Star Party with independent stargazing in Davis Mountains State Park, including altitude, timing, roads, and practical access.
- [Mont-Mégantic stargazing: ASTROLab, summit access and seasons](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/mont-megantic/): Plan a Mont-Mégantic astronomy evening through the ASTROLab, with programme reservations, summit restrictions, winter access, weather alternatives, and camping.
- [NamibRand stargazing: private-reserve access and a lodge-based night](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/namibrand/): Plan NamibRand stargazing through an authorised tourism concession, understand private-reserve boundaries and protect one of the world's darkest nightscapes.
- [Natural Bridges stargazing: a practical remote-night plan](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/natural-bridges/): Plan stargazing at Natural Bridges from the visitor-center lot or campground, with remote services, water, monsoon risk, cliff safety, and night access.
- [Stargazing in Tenerife: Teide viewpoints and a volcanic night route](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/tenerife/): Use Tenerife's official Teide astronomy route to plan a high-altitude night with legal viewpoints, realistic access checks and a self-guided sequence.
- [Uluṟu stargazing: park closing time, Yulara and a respectful night](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/uluru/): Plan Uluṟu stargazing outside the closed national park, with a Yulara base, official astrophotography guidance, cultural protocols and desert safety.
- [Warrumbungle stargazing: Camp Blackman, darkness and a safe night](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/warrumbungle/): Plan a Warrumbungle stargazing stay from Camp Blackman with booking, water, park alerts, low-light etiquette, seasonal temperatures and Siding Spring boundaries.
- [Westhavelland stargazing: official sites and a low-impact night plan](https://stargazingindex.com/en/stargazing-destinations/westhavelland/): Choose among Westhavelland's official observing sites, understand rural access and follow a practical dark-sky route built from park and tourism sources.

## Gear guides

- [Beginner telescopes compared: three 130 mm paths](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/beginner-telescopes/): A source-backed comparison of three 130 mm f/5 Newtonian systems with different mounting and transport strategies.
- [8×42 binoculars compared for stargazing](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/binoculars/): A source-backed comparison of three waterproof 8×42 roof-prism binoculars for hand-held night-sky scanning and travel.
- [Red-light headlamps compared for stargazing](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/red-flashlights/): A source-backed comparison of three rechargeable headlamps with red modes, focused on night-safe controls rather than headline white-light output.
- [Berlebach observing chairs compared: Charon, Hydra II, and Nix II](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/observing-chairs/): A source-backed comparison of three folding wooden observing chairs, focused on usable seat range, adjustment mechanism, carried mass, packed length, and support at high positions.
- [Tripods compared for binoculars and small optics](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/tripods/): A source-backed comparison of three complete tripod-and-head kits for mounted binoculars, spotting scopes, and suitably light optical loads.
- [Travel star trackers compared: three routes into tracked nightscapes](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/star-trackers/): A source-backed comparison of three portable single-axis trackers, separating bare head specifications from the wedge, counterweight, ball head, and alignment tools a field kit may still need.
- [Dew heater controllers compared: manual simplicity or sensor-led control](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/dew-control/): A source-backed comparison of three 12 V dew-controller architectures, from a two-knob manual unit to environmental sensing, five independent channels, remote control, and integrated power distribution.
- [Portable power stations compared for an astronomy field kit](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/portable-power/): A source-backed comparison of three 286–288 Wh LiFePO4 power stations, focused on the USB, regulated 12 V, and AC paths that trackers, cameras, laptops, and dew-control systems actually use.
- [11–12.5 mm telescope eyepieces compared: field, eye relief, and mass](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/eyepieces/): A source-backed comparison of three 1.25-inch eyepieces in the same medium-power focal-length band, showing what wider apparent field, longer eye relief, waterproofing, and added mass actually change.
- [CLS, UHC-E, or UHC? Three visual filter passbands compared](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/astronomy-filters/): A source-backed comparison of three Astronomik visual filters that separates their published passbands, intended targets, aperture guidance, and real limits.

## Machine-readable data

- [Dataset manifest](https://stargazingindex.com/data/stargazing/manifest.json): Dataset version, generation time, sources, counts, hashes, and checksums.
- [Destination index](https://stargazingindex.com/data/stargazing/destinations/index.json): Destination identifiers, countries, time zones, tags, and related observing sites.
- [Observation-site index](https://stargazingindex.com/data/stargazing/sites/index.json): Coordinates, elevation, access status, and source-backed access notes.
- [Editorial destination-guide index](https://stargazingindex.com/data/stargazing/editorial/destinations/index.json): Reviewed guide identifiers, word counts, source counts, and revision dates.
- [Editorial gear-guide index](https://stargazingindex.com/data/stargazing/gear/index.json): Bilingual specification comparisons with cited primary sources and dormant affiliate fields.
- [SEO registry](https://stargazingindex.com/data/stargazing/seo/registry.json): Canonicals, language alternates, descriptions, modification dates, and indexability decisions.
